equipment.name: Starlink Performance Kit (Gen 3)
equipment.blurb: Flat, ruggedised terminal for harsh environments and in-motion use. Per Starlink's specifications page: currently capable of download speeds up to 400+ Mbps, with gigabit-capable network upgrades planned (Starlink states no hardware change needed); 140° field of view, IP69K plugged in / IP68 unplugged, rated to 270+ kph winds and -40°C to 60°C, 10-year design life. Ships with an Advanced Power Supply (AC/DC, rack-mountable, battery-backup support); per Starlink's kit comparison, Performance kits do not include a WiFi router.

equipment.name: Starlink Performance (Gen 1)
equipment.blurb: Earlier Performance terminal, still listed on Starlink's specifications index; Starlink notes this kit was formerly known as the High Performance Kit. Motorised self-orienting dish, 140° field of view, IP56, snow melt up to 75 mm/hour, average power 110-150 W. Included router is WiFi 5 (802.11a/b/g/n/ac), dual-band 3x3 MIMO, coverage up to 185 m². Third-party routers connect directly at the power supply instead of using bypass mode.

equipment.name: Starlink Enterprise Kit
equipment.blurb: Business/fixed-site variant built around the Standard dish (110° field of view, IP67 Type 4, average power 75-100 W, snow melt up to 40 mm/hour) with installation flexibility: 50 m (164 ft) Enterprise cable and a choice of mount included. No router in the box — Starlink states a Starlink router can be bought separately from the Starlink Shop — because the kit is designed to connect third-party routers and custom setups directly.

equipment.name: Starlink Mesh WiFi (mesh node)

Router 3 supports up to 3 Starlink mesh nodes and the Mini is compatible with Starlink mesh systems; Starlink mesh is not compatible with third-party mesh systems. Starlink does not publish a standalone WiFi-generation figure for the node on the pages checked, so wifi is left null rather than guessed.
